name: Ninety
tagline: Team operating system for running EOS-style weekly meetings, scorecards, rocks, issues and to-dos in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Structurally this is a CRUD app with a stopwatch: a weekly agenda that walks segments on a timer, a scorecard grid of weekly numbers with red/green thresholds, quarterly rocks, an issues list you work through, and to-dos that roll over. An agent can absolutely produce that in a weekend, and for a solo operator or a three person team it will genuinely work. What it will not produce in one session is the multi user layer that makes the tool useful: accounts, roles, real time presence during the meeting, email and mobile nudges, and the accountability chart everyone can actually see. There is also the awkward part that the value here is partly social, a whole company agreeing to look at the same numbers on the same day, and your self hosted version has to earn that agreement the hard way. Build it if the team is small and you own the discipline; do not build it as a way to avoid buying seats for thirty people.
coreLoopDIY: A self hosted weekly meeting runner with a timed agenda, a scorecard of weekly metrics, quarterly rocks, an issues list and rolling to-dos, all persisted so next week starts where last week ended.
requirements: Node and a local database (SQLite is fine)
Somewhere to host it if more than one person uses it
Basic auth for teammates, or a private network
Someone willing to actually run the meeting
whatYouLose: Real time multi user meeting mode: everyone on the same screen, same timer, live cursor on the issue being solved
Mobile access and the notifications that make to-dos get done between meetings
Role based access, org wide accountability chart, and the audit trail managers like
Onboarding scaffolding and templates that match what an EOS coach will ask you for
Someone else's uptime, backups and export when your homegrown app breaks mid meeting
moatNotes: The methodology is licensed culture, not code. Companies arrive already trained on the vocabulary, and the tool wins by matching what their coach expects.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is rarely the builder. A leadership team that has paid a coach to install a management system wants software that already speaks that system, works on phones, and survives someone leaving the company. Per seat pricing on ten to forty people is cheap next to the cost of the weekly meeting itself falling apart because the internal tool nobody owns stopped syncing. The code is the easy half; the shared habit is the product.
notes: Fine for a small team that already has the discipline, pointless as a way to dodge seat costs for a big one.
prompt:
Build a self hosted team operating system app for running a weekly leadership meeting.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, Prisma with SQLite, all running locally with `npm run dev`. No external services, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data model (Prisma):
- User: name, email, role (admin or member)
- Metric: name, owner, target, comparator (gte or lte), unit
- MetricEntry: metric, weekOf (date), value
- Rock: title, owner, quarter, status (on-track, off-track, done)
- Issue: title, notes, owner, status (open, solving, solved), createdAt
- Todo: title, owner, dueDate, done
- Headline: text, kind (customer or employee), weekOf
- Meeting: date, notes, ratingAvg, segment timings as JSON

Screens:
1. Scorecard: a grid of metrics as rows and the last 13 weeks as columns. Cells editable inline. Cell turns green or red based on target and comparator. Owner shown per row.
2. Rocks: card list per quarter, click to cycle status.
3. Issues: a simple ordered list, drag to reprioritize, mark solving or solved with a resolution note.
4. To-dos: list filtered by owner, checkbox to complete, overdue items highlighted in red.
5. Meeting mode: the important screen. A fixed agenda with per segment time budgets (check-in 5, scorecard 5, rocks 5, headlines 5, to-dos 5, issues 60, wrap-up 5). A visible countdown per segment and a total elapsed clock. Next and previous segment buttons. During the issues segment, show the open issues list so items can be solved in place. On wrap-up, capture a 1 to 10 rating per attendee and save the Meeting record.

Rules:
- Auth is a single shared password from `.env` (`APP_PASSWORD`), checked in middleware. No OAuth, no user signup flow.
- Uncompleted to-dos and unsolved issues carry forward automatically to the next week. Nothing is silently deleted.
- Seed script creates 5 users, 6 metrics with 8 weeks of plausible data, 4 rocks, 6 issues, 10 to-dos.
- Include a `/api/export` route that dumps everything as JSON.

Out of scope, do not build: real time collaboration, websockets, email or push notifications, mobile app, org chart builder, file uploads, billing, multi tenancy.

Deliver a README with setup steps, the .env keys, and one paragraph on what this deliberately does not do.
